grim_lag_threshold: Two players play a prisoner's dilemma every period forever, discounting future payoffs by δ per period. Per-period payoffs: both cooperate 4 each; both defect 3 each; a defector facing a cooperator gets 6 and the cooperator gets 1. Both players use grim trigger: cooperate until a defection is discovered, then defect forever. Monitoring is imperfect: a defection in period t is only discovered at the end of period t + 2, and punishment (mutual defection forever) starts in period t + 3. Until it is discovered, the deviator keeps defecting and the other player keeps cooperating. What is the smallest discount factor δ at which no player gains by deviating from cooperation? Give δ rounded to 4 decimal places. Reply with only the number.

trust_decay_posterior:
You track an agent's reliability θ (the probability that an interaction with it goes well) with a Beta(1, 1) prior, one interaction per round. Its record, oldest first:
Round 1: good
Round 2: good
Round 3: good
Round 4: good
Round 5: good
Round 6: bad
Round 7: good
Round 8: bad
Round 9: bad
Round 10: bad
You use exponential forgetting with λ = 0.8: an interaction k rounds before the most recent one carries weight λ^k, so the most recent interaction has weight 1. With P the total weight of good interactions and N the total weight of bad ones, the posterior mean of θ is (P + 1)/(P + N + 2); the prior's pseudo-counts do not decay. What is the posterior mean of θ after round 10? Give it rounded to 4 decimal places. Reply with only the number.

oc_waterfall_junior_total: A securitisation holds a collateral pool with par balance $63,800,000. It has issued a senior tranche A of $49,400,000 paying 2% interest per period on its outstanding balance, and a junior tranche B of $8,200,000 paying 5% interest per period (B's principal is not repaid during the two periods). Equity receives whatever is left. In each of two periods, the pool collects interest of 8% of its par balance at the start of the period plus scheduled principal of $2,900,000. At the end of each period, par falls by the scheduled principal and by that period's defaults (period 1: $7,900,000; period 2: $4,000,000), with no recoveries. Each period's collections are paid in this order: (1) senior interest on tranche A's balance at the start of the period; (2) the overcollateralisation (OC) test: if end-of-period par divided by tranche A's balance is below 125%, cash is diverted to repay tranche A principal, exactly the amount that brings the ratio back to 125% (or all remaining cash if that is less); (3) junior interest on tranche B, where any shortfall is lost, not carried forward; (4) everything left goes to equity. Tranche A's balance falls only through OC diversions. What is the total cash received by junior tranche B over both periods? Give the amount in whole dollars. Reply with only the number.
